description: Add realistic film grain to iPhone photos: why Photos has no grain slider, how much grain suits portraits, street and night shots, and the fastest way.
h1: How to add film grain to a photo on iPhone
card_title: Add film grain to a photo
card_summary: Natural, film-like grain on any iPhone photo, and how much to use.
quick_answer: The Photos app has no grain or noise slider. In Halatto, open the photo and pick any look: each film or camera has its own grain built in, and you can raise or lower the grain and film age after you pick it. For a modern photo with just texture, choose a subtle look like Mini Instant, lower its strength and raise grain.
intro: Grain is the single fastest way to make a digital photo feel analog. Real film grain is not uniform noise: it is stronger in the shadows and midtones and changes with the film speed.
Here is how to add it on iPhone without the plastic, digital-noise look of a generic grain overlay.

sections.heading: Built-in options on iPhone
paragraphs: Photos' Edit tools (Exposure, Contrast, Noise Reduction and others) can remove noise but not add grain. Some recent iPhone models offer a film-style texture in the Camera's Photographic Styles for new shots; check Camera > Styles on yours. Neither works on photos you have already taken.
Pro editors like Lightroom have a Grain slider with amount, size and roughness. Halatto ties the grain to a film or camera, so it matches the color and lens of the look.

steps.heading: Step by step: grain in Halatto

items.name: Open the photo
items.text: Pick a photo in Halatto or share it from Photos.

items.name: Pick a look
items.text: Choose a film look from the Looks strip; its grain is applied with it.

items.name: Set grain and film age
items.text: Raise grain for a faster, coarser film; raise film age for fade and wear.

items.name: Check at 100%
items.text: Pinch to zoom in on a face or a shadow to see if the grain looks natural.

items.name: Save
items.text: Save or share. Grain survives compression best on photos you send at full size.

tips.heading: Tips
items: Social apps compress photos; add a little more grain than looks right on your screen.
Grain hides iPhone over-sharpening and HDR halos.
Black and white photos take heavy grain better than color ones.

faq.question: Is grain the same as noise?
faq.answer: Not quite. Digital noise is colored and blotchy; film grain is finer and follows the tones of the image. Digicam looks in Halatto add noise on purpose; film looks add grain.

faq.question: Can I add grain without changing the colors?
faq.answer: Pick a subtle look and lower its strength, then raise grain. The color shift becomes minimal while the grain stays.

faq.question: Does grain reduce photo quality?
faq.answer: It adds texture rather than removing detail, and the original stays in your library.
